name: Metal bottles/tumblers
anchor: EU food-contact framework Regulation 1935/2004 with Regulation (EU) 10/2011 Annex II specific migration limits as the only element-migration instrument in the register expressed in the food-contact FOOD basis (the register's other migration instruments — the EU 2009/48 toy Categories I to III and the ASTM F963 soluble limits — are in the toy article-extraction basis and are barred from every row of this category). Rows whose principal food-contact surface is a polymer anchor it directly, or by disclosed read-across where the instrument's own scope article excludes or does not reach the material or where the taxonomy row also carries a non-plastic configuration. Metal, alloy, ceramic-glaze, vitreous-enamel and glass rows, and the two water-treatment-device rows, are controls because their dedicated release regimes (Directive 84/500/EEC as amended by 2005/31/EC, the metals-and-alloys release regime, and the drinking-water device route) are not in the register in their own jurisdictions' rows. Where one taxonomy row carries both a polymer and a metal configuration, the published cells take the metal-article control and the plastics value is disclosed as a film-only companion.
cross_reference: Category 9 (Infant and Child Contact Products) governs any article in this row that is marketed for ages 0-5; the taxonomy boundary rule routes infant bottles, nipples and toddler drinkware there even though they are food-contact items.
native_basis: element release from the food-contact alloy into food or food simulant (µg/kg food)
native_basis_label: element RELEASE FROM THE FOOD-CONTACT ALLOY INTO FOOD OR A FOOD SIMULANT, µg/kg of food, determined against an acidic simulant at the article's stated use temperature and duration with the third successive release governing for repeat-use articles. This is a RELEASE basis on the food, not the plastics-simulant convention and not a total-content basis: the percent-by-weight lead limits on food-contact metals and solder are a separate MATERIAL-CONTENT obligation, disclosed as companions and never published here.
scope_note: Reusable metal drink containers. The food-contact surface is the interior alloy or its liner. The characteristic pathway is not the wall alloy but the BASE PLUG of a vacuum-insulated body, where a lead-bearing solder or braze seals the evacuation port and becomes an exposure route only if the covering cap detaches; that is the subject of well-known consumer-product recalls and Proposition 65 actions and is why the component plan requires the base to be tested and its cover retention verified as a mechanical requirement. No credible sovereign sets an element release ceiling for a metal food-contact article, so the row is a control; the Japanese and Korean percent-by-weight lead limits on food-contact metals and solder are disclosed as MATERIAL-CONTENT companions. TRACEABILITY OF THE COMPONENT POINTER: where this row's component plan refers a plastic component to "the plastics migration ceilings", that phrase resolves to a concrete published set of values inside this same standard and is not an unresolved pointer. It means the Reg (EU) 10/2011 Annex II values published on this category's plastics rows — eu_10_2011_pb_sml_nd (lead, not detectable at 10 ug/kg food), eu_10_2011_cd_sml_nd (cadmium, 2), eu_10_2011_tas_sml_nd (total arsenic, 10), eu_10_2011_thg_sml_nd (total mercury, 10), eu_10_2011_ni_sml (nickel, 20), eu_10_2011_al_sml (aluminium, 1000) and eu_10_2011_crtotal_sml_nd (total chromium, not detectable at 10), with tin excepted because the instrument lists no tin entry. Those values bind the plastic component as a SEPARATE obligation in its own material family and are never this row's published ceiling, which stays in this row's own native basis.
material: Single- and double-wall austenitic stainless steel and aluminium bottles and tumblers; interior lacquer or ceramic-coated liners on some aluminium bottles; vacuum-insulated bodies closed with a soldered or welded base plug; painted or powder-coated exteriors; plastic and silicone lids, straws and gaskets.
components: Sample and report separately: (1) interior wall alloy, acidic-simulant release at the highest claimed hold temperature and duration; (2) interior lacquer or ceramic liner where fitted, which is a coating and takes the polymeric or ceramic regime of its own family; (3) BASE PLUG solder or braze, analysed for lead content and tested for release with the cover removed, plus a cover-retention verification; (4) threaded neck, cut edges and any weld; (5) lid, gasket, straw and bite valve, bound by the plastics migration ceilings directly or by disclosed read-across; (6) exterior paint or powder coat, tested as a mouth-and-hand-contact surface at the lip.
basis_guard: element release|specific release|specific release limit|release into food|release into a food simulant|release into the food simulant|acetic acid
basis_guard_note: Only an instrument expressed as element RELEASE from a metal or alloy food-contact surface into food or a food simulant may anchor a cell on this row. The guard exists to reject the three foreign bases that surround this category and would otherwise look plausible: the FOOD basis (canned-food tin maximum levels, which limit the contents and not the article), the MATERIAL-CONTENT basis (CPSIA total lead in substrate, EU REACH Annex XVII cadmium percent-by-weight restrictions, RoHS homogeneous-material limits, Japan Notice 370 and Korea MFDS percent-by-weight lead in food-contact metals), and the ARTICLE-EXTRACTION basis of the toy regime (EU 2009/48 Annex II Part III and ASTM F963 soluble limits, which are element migration from scraped-off or coated TOY material into 0.07 M hydrochloric acid, expressed per kg of MATERIAL, not per kg of food). Any of those would fail this guard and resolve to a gap rather than publish in the wrong basis. On this control row the guard is declaratory as well as operative: it records the only basis in which a future ingested instrument would be allowed to supply this row's numbers, so that a content limit, a food limit, a water limit or a plastics specific migration limit cannot later be dropped in as this row's release ceiling. The plastics clause is deliberately absent from this guard: a Reg (EU) 10/2011 value named here would fail the guard and resolve to a gap. DECLARED VACUOUS STATE (recorded, not overlooked): as written this guard matches ZERO live, non-draft and non-quarantined rows in data/evidence/regulatory_limits.csv, and that is its intended state. The release regime this row's basis family belongs to is not in the register in any form this row may bind, which is the same fact this row's control cells record and state in detail; a guard that admitted a live row today could only do so by admitting a foreign basis. The guard is nevertheless expressed in the register's own basis vocabulary (element or specific release, release into food or a food simulant, 4 percent acetic acid extract, per dm2 of food-contact surface, net device contribution to the treated water) so that a future correct ingest of that regime BINDS through it. The previous prose-sentence guard on this row would have REJECTED the very instruments it was waiting for and forced them to a gap, which is the defect this rewrite removes. Two limits on the guard's force are stated plainly rather than left implicit: the compiler returns on the control branch before basis resolution, so a guard is never evaluated on a control cell, and this note rather than the machine is what carries the guard's force on this row today. The engine change that would close that hole - an assertion that every declared basis_guard either matches at least one live register row or carries basis_guard_vacuous_by_design, failing the build otherwise - is recorded as a tooling gap and is outside this config's scope.
method: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit-only): the strictest applicable sovereign maximum for this exact product form expressed as specific element migration into food or a food simulant; a disclosed read-across from the nearest applicable sovereign value in the same basis where the food-contact material family is expressly excluded from or not reached by that instrument; a substantiated not-material determination; or a control. No cell is occurrence-derived, and no cell borrows a value across a basis.

Pb.rationale: No sovereign sets a food-RELEASE (migration) lead limit for bare-metal food-contact articles in the register. The KR MFDS metal-FCM value is an alloy-COMPOSITION spec (percent by weight), not a release-into-food limit, so it is not adopted here. Proper source: China GB 4806.9-2016 metal-FCM migration limits / CoE CM/Res(2013)9 (pending addition to the register).

Cr.rationale: No credible sovereign sets a numeric ceiling on element release from a metal or alloy food-contact article. Regulation (EU) 10/2011 governs plastics only; metals and alloys are a separate Regulation 1935/2004 Annex I material family for which the EU has adopted no specific measure, the US regulates food-contact substances without an element release ceiling, and Codex, FSANZ, Health Canada, the UK and Hong Kong set none. Testing is therefore mandatory on every certified lot with no invented ceiling: a limit borrowed from the plastics regulation would be a limit written for a different material family, and for an alloy surface the plastics nickel and aluminium values are not even achievable, so borrowing them would be an unfounded number rather than a stricter one. Total chromium is retained as a screening determination for the alloy-release pathway rather than as a toxicological ceiling: chromium released from austenitic stainless steel is overwhelmingly chromium(III), which is the benign species, so a total-chromium number on this row would not be protective even if a sovereign had set one. The health-relevant determination is the hexavalent-chromium cell. On a vacuum-insulated bottle the binding component is the base-plug solder or braze, not the wall alloy; a wall-only result does not represent the article and is not accepted.
Cr.reference_method: Food-simulant release testing on each food-contact metal component under worst foreseeable use conditions (acidic simulant at the article's stated cooking or holding temperature and duration; for repeat-use articles the third successive release result governs), ICP-MS determination in the simulant, plus alloy-composition verification of every food-contact component by ICP-OES after acid digestion (XRF for screening only).
